_what: Reference values to audit Nicolas's calibration answers against. Three independent sources per movement where they exist.

_sources.research: memory/calisthenics_benchmarks_research.md — triangulated from Calisthenic Movement, FitnessFAQs, Hybrid Calisthenics, GMB, Bodyweight Warrior, StrengthLevel, GainStrong, TopEndSports, ATHLEAN-X, Bodyweight Tribe. Cali-specific, male values, 3 tiers.
_sources.csv: FOR NICOLAS/BENCHMARKS - Male.csv — the in-repo rank table, 4 tiers (Beg/Int/Adv/Elite), max-test standards.
_sources.web: Fresh 2026-08 searches, cited per row in the notes.

_units: reps unless the row says secs

Push-ups.note: ACSM: untrained men 18-39 average 13-29 strict; 'excellent' 29+ at age 30. Trained 30-50. Serious calisthenics 50+. 75 is elite, not advanced.

Pull-Up.note: StrengthLevel average male 14. GainStrong intermediate 8-12. ATHLEAN-X 15 at age 30. Research beginner=3 assumes someone who just got their first; CSV beginner=8 assumes someone who already trains.

Wide Inverted Row.note: Bodyweight Tribe beginner 3x10. Both references sit well above the entered 5/15/30.

Pike Push-Up.note: Bodyweight Warrior intermediate 10. The two references agree closely.

Handstand Push-Up.note: Full-ROM freestanding. CSV's Wall HSPU (0/5/10) is a different, easier movement.

Ring Dip.note: Harder than bar dip; scaled down from it.

Bodyweight Squat.note: All three agree. Bodyweight Tribe intermediate 3x100.

Burpee.note: Research figures are PER MINUTE, not per set. A max unbroken set is a different test.

Forearm Plank.note: McGill's lab treats ~2 min as the meaningful ceiling; Dan John: 'a maximum of 2 minutes, anything longer is meaningless.' Past that it tests pain tolerance, not core capacity. The CSV's 300s is the outlier.

Hollow Hold.note: Gymnastics standard treats a solid 60s as strong. The CSV is aggressive.

Dead Hang.note: Consensus: most healthy adults 30-60s; 60s a good target; 90s+ elite. Longevity guidance: 2 min for a 40-year-old man. Research column matches the consensus best.

V-Sit.note: HARDER than the L-sit — legs and hips rise higher, more compression and hamstring flexibility. Prerequisite is a clean 10s straight-leg L-sit. Its numbers must therefore be LOWER than the L-sit's, not higher.

Hanging Leg Raise.note: CSV's Toes-to-Bar (5/10/20) is the harder cousin and lands in the same range.

Dragon Flag (Tuck).note: Research covers full Dragon Flag in reps (0/3/8), not the tuck hold. No conflict.

Freestanding HS.note: Research advanced 90s is a genuine hand-balancer. 30s is closer to a solid intermediate.

Full Front Lever.note: Research covers TUCK front lever (0/10/25). Full lever at 5-10s advanced is consistent with every cali source.

Muscle-Up (Bar).note: Consensus: ~10 strict pull-ups is the prerequisite; 3-5 = intermediate; 8-10 = advanced.

Weighted Chin-Up.note: The LOAD is the level here, not the reps. Common standard: +25% bodyweight for 5 = strong, +50% for 1 = advanced. A flat 20 kg across all three tiers cannot be right.

Archer Pull-Up.note: Left blank; roughly half your pull-up number per side.

Deep Squat Rocks.note: Left blank — mobility, arguably should not be calibrated at all.

Tuck L-Sit.note: Left blank; easier than the L-sit, so above its numbers.

Thoracic Rotations.note: Left blank — mobility, not a capacity test.

Bulgarian Split Squat.note: Left blank. Both references agree exactly.

Farmer's Carry (no straps).note: Left blank. CSV rates it by load: 0.5/1.0/1.5x bodyweight total for 20m.

Kettlebell Swing.note: Left blank. CSV rates by load: 0.2/0.3/0.45x bodyweight.
